title: Exam Plan ignores its own 'h a week': at '1 h a week' every week is planned at 2 h (3 h in the last week)
detail: An F201 real exam (12 Jan 2027) on the dense account, Plan section, budget select at '1 h a week' (the header reads '1 h a week for Real exam'). KOS.examSession.schedule(a) places 60 min in the first week, then 120 min in each of the next five weeks (topic 30 + paper 90) and 180 min in the week of 4 Jan (topic 30, paper 90, redo 30, cheat sheet 30). Week cards print '2 h 00' / '3 h 00' under a header promising 1 h. Send to the plan writes those rows into Pacing as they are. Reproduced twice (eval and the Plan screenshot). Expected: a paper that does not fit the week's hours is not placed (or the week shows that it is over, and the header's figure is the planned one).
rootCause: js/core/examsession.js:464 — `if (fits(d, pm) || !d.items.length) place(...)`: a paper is placed whenever its day is empty, even when `fits` says the week's minutes are spent; the redo, cheat-sheet and night-before items (458–460) are placed with no `fits` check at all.
fix: Drop the `|| !d.items.length` escape (or only allow it when the week has nothing yet and say 'over by n min' on the week card); run the fixed last-week items through `fits` too, or show the plan's real weekly total beside the budget.

title: An authored F201 practice paper's side panel calls the papers 'Predicted paper 1/2/3', lists the paper you are on, and describes it as a shape-weighted draw
detail: Open #/exams/<F201>/paper/2 (or /1, /3). The 'Another paper' card offers 'Predicted paper 1 ›', 'Predicted paper 2 ›' (the paper already open) and 'Predicted paper 3 ›'. F201 has no Companion, so nothing is predicted (invariant 130: only a full Companion makes a predicted paper); the papers are the authored 'Practice paper 1 · Coastline Energy', '2 · Calderford City Council', '3 · Freshway'. 'Where the questions come from' says 'Original questions written by KurenaiOS for this paper's question shapes, weighted to its high-yield topics and to the shapes due by their pattern … The mark scheme names each question's shape' — none of which is true of an authored paper. 'This paper' says 'about 10 questions a sitting' for an 8-question paper. On paper 4 (a bank draw) the list correctly omits nothing but calls the authored papers just 'Practice paper 1/2/3'. Reproduced on papers 1 and 2, cold and warm.
rootCause: js/modules/exampaperview.js:110-117 — the side panel only knows 'practice' vs everything else, so kind 'authored' takes the predicted wording; the seed filter `n !== paper.seed` compares a number with the authored paper's string seed (js/core/exampaper.js:137 `seed: String(n)`), so the current paper is never excluded.
evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/exams-files-ink/paper-f201-2-mac-dense.png; eval on /paper/1 → typeof seed 'string', seed buttons ['Predicted paper 1','Predicted paper 2','Predicted paper 3']
fix: Give 'authored' its own branch: 'Written whole by KurenaiOS in the board's format — not a board paper', title each link from KOS.examPaper.authoredList (e.g. 'Practice paper 2 · Calderford City Council'), compare seeds as numbers, and use bp.questions only for drawn papers.
phase1: 1B (c0c67c39) — papers 2 and 3 made the list three authored papers

title: At 700 px and under (phone, iPad Split View and Slide Over) an exam's header actions vanish with no substitute, and a deep-linked Papers/Plan/Questions section draws under the Cards row
detail: iphone 402, split 590, slide 375, dense account, F201 exam. On every section the header's 'Edit scope', '＋ Log a result' and '⋯' (the exam's Edit/Archive/Delete) measure 0×0; on Revise the header's 'Card drill' and '⎙ Print the guide' are gone; on a sat paper (#/exams/<id>/paper/2) '‹ Papers' is 0×0. The only ways round are the All exams list (its row ⋯ and its own '＋ Log a result'). The phone list shows Today, Topics, Revise, Cards and Review (D5), but on an iPad in Split View the same rules apply, so the device the Papers are for loses them. Opening #/exams/<id>/papers at 590 (a link from Today's paper card, search or Home) draws the Papers list directly under the 'Cards · 0 due' row, as if it were the Cards section's content, with no Papers row. Reproduced at iphone and split, twice each.
rootCause: css/views/exams.css:1238 — `@media (max-width: 700px) { .k-xs-head .k-ex-actions { display: none; } }` hides the whole action slot (js/modules/examshell.js:260-272 puts every action, and the paper view's '‹ Papers' from js/modules/exampaperview.js:80, in it); js/modules/examshell.js:39 `PHONE` lists only today/topics/revise/cards/review, so a non-phone section's body has no row of its own and lands after the last row drawn (344).
evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/exams-files-ink/exam-f201-today-iphone-dense.png; /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/exams-files-ink/exam-f201-papers-split-dense.png; eval at iphone: Edit scope 0x0, ＋ Log a result 0x0, ⋯ 0x0, exams.paper-back 0x0
fix: Keep the action slot on the phone as one ⋯ menu (Edit scope, Log a result, Edit, Archive, Delete, and the section's own actions such as Card drill and Print); when a non-phone section is open at ≤700 px give it its own row (or redirect to Today with the 'Papers · on the iPad and Mac' note), and let Split View on a touch iPad keep Papers.

title: F201 papers: the '(b)(i)' label breaks over two lines and '(ii)' repeats '(b)', on screen and in print
detail: Every authored F201 paper (1, 2 and 3) has a linked (i)/(ii) part in question 7 labelled '(b)(i)' and '(b)(ii)'. The label column is one '(a)' wide, so the sheet prints '(b)' on one line and '(i)' on the next, then '(b)' again over '(ii)'. OCR's format (invariant 127, ocr-case: 'lettered and (i)/(ii) parts') prints '(b) (i)' once and '(ii)' alone. Seen in the A4 print of papers 1–3 (sheet 9) and on the same sheet on screen.
rootCause: js/modules/exampaperview.js:252 draws `p.label` whole in the fixed-width label cell; the data (js/data/exams/papers/ocr-f201-1.js:193/196, -2.js:190/193, -3.js:189/193) carries the parent letter in both labels.
fix: In the label cell print a (ii) whose (i) sits just before it as '(ii)' alone, and let the cell take '(b) (i)' on one line (min-content width or nowrap).
